btc-long-2025-10.name: Bitcoin
btc-long-2025-10.lede: The last long of the 2025 bull market: built on the 107–110k support from 17 October, averaged down into 100–103k, and cut at the invalidation on 14 November — one day before the public bear-market call. Flat to a small loss, exactly as the plan said it would be if the level failed.

chapters.h: The first long orders fill in the 107–110k support
chapters.p: After hedging the 10 October crash from 120k and re-entering at 102k, the first orders of a fresh long were filled in the 107–110k region. The target was the fair-value gap at 118–120k; orders were kept lower, under the golden line, to hunt wicks in the 97–100k region if the market offered them.
The plan in four lines: build the long at 107–110k, add at 97–100k if allowed, first target 118–120k, then the liquidity pool at 140–150k.

chapters.h: Average entry $107,750 — targets and invalidation restated
chapters.p: With the market unpricing the December rate cut, the orders at 97–100k were pulled and some of that cash added to the position below 110k, moving the average to $107,750. The rules were written down: hold until the take profit at 118–120k or the invalidation; a retest of the EMA50 weekly at 97–100k possible but not expected.
The $100,000 level was being defended. Serious size was queued in the 100–103k region to add if the market visited it.

chapters.h: Orders filled: the average drops to $101,350
chapters.p: The scam wicks into 100–103k filled the orders. Average long price $101,350, remaining orders at $100,150 and $100,350, target unchanged at $118,000–120,000.
The last orders were hit as price kissed 100k. Time to bounce — or to be proven wrong at the invalidation.
Short term the market looked ready for 100–101k, so a separate 40× isolated long was opened at $98,163 with a tight stop.

chapters.h: The scalp prints over $650,000 within three hours
chapters.p: Three hours later the 40× position showed more than $650,000 of profit.

chapters.h: Invalidation hit — the longs are closed in a small loss
chapters.p: The weekly structure broke. The longs were closed near $100,500 in a small loss, exactly at the invalidation written down weeks earlier. Status after the exit: 50% short stocks, 40% cash, 10% physical watches and gold.
The same afternoon the structure was declared broken and the bear market confirmed: sell Bitcoin near 100k before the drop toward 50k. The next day the public call followed at 94k.

chapters.h: The full accounting of the year
chapters.p: For the record, every entry and exit of 2025 in one post: bought 76k, sold 110k; bought 100k, sold 120k; bought 102k, sold 116k; bought 107k, 102k and 98k, sold near 100,500. The last long left at breakeven or a small loss — which, on the whole sequence, is the same as having sold at 120k.

btc-long-2025-12.name: Bitcoin
btc-long-2025-12.lede: A bear-market long, opened on purpose: the value area low at 80–84k had to be bought because market makers needed a bull trap before the next leg down. Triggered at $84,550 on 18 December, closed at $95,350 on 14 January — and the short that replaced it the same day became the trade of the year.

chapters.p: Mid-term bearish, short-term bullish: the plan was to buy the value area low, take profits in the 98–104k region and open a big short there. Next big move after that: 68–74k.
The orders filled the day before at $84,550. The long would be held until the retest of the EMA50 weekly, with small orders kept lower in the value area low.
Every open position and every resting order published in one list: the BTC long from $84,550, the stock shorts from November, the sell-and-short orders at $98,350 and $103,650.

chapters.h: Why the long exists inside a bear market
chapters.p: Accumulation at 80–84k, distribution expected above the EMA50 weekly, a local top around March–April and then the leg to 64–70k. The long was a trade on the bull trap, not a change of mind.

chapters.h: Up more than 10% from the entry
chapters.p: Two and a half weeks after the fill, Bitcoin traded more than 10% above $84,550. The script — pump to trap bulls, then the move down — was playing out.

chapters.h: The long is closed and the first short opens
chapters.p: Too many people were waiting for 98–104k to short. The long was closed at $95,350 and the first short order opened at the same price — earlier than the original plan, to not miss the move.

chapters.h: In writing: longed $84,550, closed $95,350 in big profits
chapters.p: The Sunday post put the numbers on the record and set the rest of the plan: short orders from 98k to 104k in 1k steps, target 64–70k.

btc-short-2026-01.name: Bitcoin
btc-short-2026-01.lede: The trade of the bear market. Opened at $95,350 on 14 January, two weeks before the Option A breakdown, and closed at $64,750 on 23 February: a 32% move in the price, +$640,485 on the posted position.

chapters.p: The long from $84,550 was closed and the short started the same minute. 95k was already a good level when the destination was below 70k.

chapters.h: The ladder above: short orders at 98k, 99k … 104k
chapters.p: Orders were added at every thousand from 98k to 104k, to add size if the market offered Option B — a last visit to the 98–104k zone. The $95,350 short was to be held with diamond hands.

Mid-term target 64–70k, head-and-shoulders on the weekly, bankrupt market makers still forced to sell. All USDT and USDC in the wallets were to be used to short Bitcoin until there was no room left on the downside.

chapters.h: Positioning summary with every signal linked
chapters.p: The first full positioning post: BTC short from $95,350, the stock and index shorts, and the pending orders — every line with a link to the original call as execution proof.

chapters.h: Bitcoin at $82,308 — “remember those who mocked me for shorting at 95k”
chapters.p: Two weeks in and 13% lower, with Option A (straight down) gaining probability over Option B (one more pump to 98–104k). Target unchanged: 64–70k.

chapters.h: Option A confirmed; a second, short-term short in a sub-account
chapters.p: As $80,600 broke, a short-term leveraged short was opened in a sub-account and shared live; the big position from 95k stayed in the main account. The screenshot shows the main short at +132% on the margin.
From 80k the call was a pump to 98k and a major leg down; the long was taken at 80k, closed at 95k, the short opened there and held. Bitcoin at 70k, with the account statement posted as proof.
Four minutes after the relief-bounce long opened, the short from 95k was closed. The statement shows 21 BTC short from $95,225.8, mark $64,726.4, profit $640,485.61.
“I shorted at $95,000 and took profits at $64,750, just to take profits at $68,000 and flip short again.”

btc-long-2026-02.name: Bitcoin
btc-long-2026-02.lede: The second bear-market long: opened at $64,750 the minute the 95k short was closed, sized up at 63–64k and 67,750, and closed in profit around $68,000 on 31 March — the day before the short was re-opened.

chapters.p: The monthly value area low at 63k was the edge entry, but the market was gaining strength and the long was opened at $64,753 rather than risk missing it. A high-risk long by design — short-term bullish inside a bear market.

chapters.h: The 63–64k support is tested — heavy size added
chapters.p: The support was tested the next night and heavy size was added to the position.
Active: BTC long $64,750, ETH long $1,940, the stock and index shorts. The plan to flip short at 77–79k, 81–83k and 85–87k was published the same evening.
After the Iran-headline dip, another long was added at $67,750. Current longs: $64,750 and $67,750, invalidation at $66,000 (later moved to orderbook acceptance below 62k).

chapters.h: The 65k order fills on the bounce
chapters.p: Long orders at 65k were filled overnight and Bitcoin was up 4% from there by morning; orders at 63k and 64k stayed in place.

chapters.h: Position update: ETH and BTC longs closed in profit
chapters.p: As stocks pumped and oil dumped on something happening behind closed doors, both longs were closed in profit and the book went fully hedged — short stocks, flat crypto.
The next morning: “took profits at $68,000 and flip short again. Ready for more downside.”

eth-long-2026-03.name: Ethereum
eth-long-2026-03.lede: A beta trade on the Bitcoin bounce: long ETH at $1,940 on 9 March, partial profits at $2,350 eight days later, the rest closed with the BTC long on 31 March.

chapters.h: ETH long at $1,938 — “this trade has to be taken”
chapters.p: With Bitcoin at the last value area low and the US–Iran panic priced in, a 15–20% pump in ETH was expected if the value areas held. From a risk-reward standpoint the trade had to be taken.
ETH behaved exactly as expected and moved with Bitcoin; part of the position was closed around $2,350, +21% from the entry.

chapters.h: The rest is closed with the Bitcoin long
chapters.p: Both longs were closed in profit on 31 March as the book went hedged.

oil-long-2026-04.name: WTI crude oil
oil-long-2026-04.lede: A short, clean commodity trade: oil bought at $92.50 on 16 April expecting $110–120 on escalation, profits taken at $97 on 27 April — +5% in eleven days.

chapters.p: With the Strait of Hormuz closed again and oil far from its earlier $120 panic, a spot buy at $92.50 expecting $110–120 next.
Eleven days later the long was closed at $97 with a 5% ROI on the spot buy.

btc-short-2026-04.name: Bitcoin
btc-short-2026-04.lede: The continuation of the 95k short. Re-opened at $68,000 on 1 April, held through the 82k pump (“early, but not wrong”) and the June slide, and covered at about $64,000 on 11 August — the same minute the first spot Bitcoin was bought.

chapters.p: After taking profits on the long, the short was re-opened at $68,000: “Ready for more downside!”
The positioning summary records the short at $68,000 as the resume of the initial short opened at $95,000 and closed at $64,000, with orders to add at 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k.
Two months later, with Bitcoin back in the 60s: shorts from 95k, 81k, 79k and 77k all in profit; profits to be taken only below 60k.
The take profits on every short were placed exactly where the spot buy orders sat, so each short closed would become a spot buy.
Short-term noise did not change the mid-term position: the shorts were to be held and the take profits kept at 53–45k.
With exchanges filing for bankruptcy and retail selling in losses, the view changed: no further big downside, buy spot and close shorts in the 54–60k region only.
Buying Bitcoin spot in the 54–60k region only; taking profits on shorts in the same region only.

chapters.h: Shorts closed, spot bought — for the first time since the top
chapters.p: Prices refused to go lower, so the shorts were closed and spot was bought at market, around $64,072: “the long awaited bull is very close to start.”

btc-short-77-83k.name: Bitcoin
btc-short-77-83k.lede: One position, added to three times. The short ladder for Q2 was set on 23 March at 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k; the 77k rung filled on 17 April, 79k on 22 April and 81.5k on 5 May, the 83k order never did. Held through the sideways summer and covered at about $64,072 on 11 August, the day the first spot Bitcoin was bought — about +19% on the average entry.

chapters.h: The ladder is set: short orders at 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k
chapters.p: While still long from 63–64k, the short orders for Q2 were placed above the range: 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k, with take profits drawn at 50k, 45k and 40k.
Bitcoin tested the range highs and the 77k order was the first of the ladder to fill, at $77,498.5.
Five days later the 79k rung filled at $79,434; the 81k and 83k orders stayed above. “Say what you want — 45k is coming this year.”
On 5 May a further rung was added at $81,504, leaving one last order at 83k that never filled.
By early June Bitcoin was back in the 60s and every rung of the ladder was in profit. Profits to be taken only below 60k.

chapters.h: Everyone who shorted the 77–83k region printed heavily
chapters.p: Nothing is more profitable than mid-term trading, and the only thing needed is patience.

chapters.h: Take profits moved to the spot buy levels
chapters.p: Take-profit orders on all shorts moved to 53k, 51k, 49k, 47k and 45k — the same levels as the spot buy orders.
Prices never reached the ladder's take profits; on 11 August the shorts were closed and spot was bought at market around $64,072.

btc-short-77-83k.headline: Short Bitcoin from 77k to 81.5k

btc-short-77k.name: Bitcoin
btc-short-77k.lede: One rung of the short ladder set on 23 March at 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k. Filled at 77k on 17 April, held through the sideways summer and covered at about $64,072 on 11 August.

chapters.h: The ladder is set: short orders at 77k, 79k, 81k and 83k

eth-short-2026-04.name: Ethereum
eth-short-2026-04.lede: Shorted at $2,350 on 14 April with a 70% crash called, held for four months and covered at about $1,879 on 11 August — a 20% move in the price — into the first spot ETH of the new cycle.

chapters.p: Into the April pump: “SHORTING $2,350 — CRASH COMING FOR ETH — I CALL NOW A 70% CRASH.”

chapters.h: Targets: $1,400, then the 2022 cycle bottom at $880
chapters.p: With ETH losing every support of its range, the April lows at $1,400 became the next target and the 2022 low the final one.
ETH at about $1,879: the short was closed and spot bought the same minute as Bitcoin.

pltr-short-2025-11.name: Palantir
pltr-short-2025-11.lede: The stock short of the year. Opened at $207 on 4 November 2025 — the exact top — added at $187 in December, and closed at about $128 on 19 June 2026, +40% as posted, to move the capital into Bitcoin. The stock was later bought back at $125–130.

chapters.h: Adding Palantir to the shorts at $207
chapters.p: Minutes after shorting the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, Palantir joined the list at $207.18. “Please do yourself a favor and don't make the mistake of fading these calls.”

chapters.h: Down more than 10% the next day
chapters.p: Twenty-four hours later the stock traded at $182: “Overvalued stock only deserves to be shorted with full force.”
PLTR −15%, NVDA −10%, AMD −10%, TSLA −7% since the short calls; META, MSFT, SPX and NDX −3%.
Nine days in: “We started shorting at $207 last week and it's already at $178. If we see a relief bounce I will add more size.”
Shorts triggered in the full top at $207; three take-profit zones drawn down to about $50, where the position would be fully closed and flipped long.
On the December relief bounce more size was added at $187, a month after the first short at $207.

chapters.h: Taking profits: +40% since the short entry
chapters.p: Seven and a half months later the short was closed with the stock around $128, to release liquidity for Bitcoin spot. The chart posted shows the move since the entry.

nvda-short-2025-11.name: Nvidia
nvda-short-2025-11.lede: The AI-bubble short that did not play out: Nvidia shorted at $207 on 4 November, added at $187 on 8 December, and closed at breakeven on 19 June when the capital was moved to Bitcoin.

chapters.h: Adding Nvidia to the shorts at $207
chapters.p: Shorted at $206.88 the same hour as Palantir, with the stock market top called.

chapters.h: SoftBank sells its whole stake — stock at $194
chapters.p: A week later, with SoftBank out of its entire $5.83bn position: “It was the correct move to short this stock one week ago at $207. Current price is $194. Next big move below $100.”
The thesis in one chart: the AI bubble has to burst before the next move higher; more size only above the entry.

chapters.h: Shorting more at $187 — a sell-the-news event
chapters.p: The euphoria on simple news smelled like exit liquidity; more was shorted at $187 after the initial $207.
On 19 June the Nvidia short was closed at breakeven, with the AMD and Intel shorts closed at a small loss, to put everything into Bitcoin.

amd-short-2025-11.name: AMD
amd-short-2025-11.lede: Part of the 4 November basket: AMD shorted at $259.65 alongside Tesla, Meta and Microsoft. Down 10% within two days, back above the entry by June, closed at a small loss on 19 June.

chapters.h: Adding to shorts: AMD at $259, TSLA $468, META $637, MSFT $517
chapters.p: The second wave of the stock-market short, an hour after the index shorts.
The Nvidia shadow was expected to be punished over the following months, with the gaps below as targets.
Released on 19 June together with Intel, at a small loss, as the liquidity went to Bitcoin spot.

tsla-short-2025-11.name: Tesla
tsla-short-2025-11.lede: Shorted at $468.31 on 4 November as part of the basket, with the note that Tesla was extremely bullish long term and only deserved a short for the correction. Closed on 19 June around $400: +20% as posted.

chapters.p: Shorted with AMD, Meta and Microsoft in the second wave of the 4 November call.

chapters.h: Bullish long term, short for now
chapters.p: “I see Tesla easily becoming a multi-trillion dollar company in the future. Nevertheless it is extremely bearish short term and deserves to be shorted.”
Closed on 19 June at about $400 with the chart of the move since the short.

meta-short-2025-11.name: Meta
meta-short-2025-11.lede: A nine-day short: Meta at $637.71 on 4 November, about 3% lower two days later, closed on 13 November with Microsoft to rotate the capital into a bigger S&P 500 short.

chapters.p: Part of the second wave of the stock-market short: AMD $259, TSLA $468, META $637, MSFT $517.
Two days later the basket was all red; Meta, Microsoft and the indices about 3% below the entries.

chapters.h: Closed — capital rotated into the S&P short
chapters.p: “Closing MSFT and META shorts and rotating that capital into more short in the SPX.”

msft-short-2025-11.name: Microsoft
msft-short-2025-11.lede: A nine-day short: Microsoft at $517.03 on 4 November, closed on 13 November about 3% lower, with the capital moved into the S&P 500 short. The same stock was bought back at $385 in July.

chapters.p: Part of the second wave of the stock-market short.
Two days later Meta, Microsoft, SPX and NDX were about 3% below the entries.

chapters.h: Closed — capital rotated into the S&P short
chapters.p: “Closing MSFT and META shorts and rotating that capital into more short in the SPX.”

spx-short-2025-11.name: S&P 500
spx-short-2025-11.lede: The index short behind the November top call. Opened at 6,851.98 on 4 November 2025, added at 6,950 on 14 April, and closed at a small loss on 19 June. The exit that should have been taken at 6,300 after the 10% correction was not — admitted in writing on 5 August.

chapters.p: The first order of the day: “Shorting #SPX here”, with the index at 6,851.98. The call for the top of the stock market followed within the hour.
The status post after two sessions: the single names −7 to −15%, the indices −3%.
The index that tracks the 500 largest companies remained extremely overvalued; a 15–20% correction was still the expectation.
On the April ceasefire pump more was added at $6,950.
The SPX, NDX and NI225 shorts were released at a small loss on 19 June: all liquidity had to flow into Bitcoin spot.

With the S&P at fresh highs: “While the Bitcoin short was massively profitable, the SP500 short wasn't because I failed to call the exit at $6,300 after a 10% correction. I admit I should have called the exit there.”

ndx-short-2025-11.name: Nasdaq 100
ndx-short-2025-11.lede: Shorted at 25,972.94 nineteen minutes after the S&P 500 on 4 November 2025 and released at a small loss on 19 June 2026 with the other index shorts.

chapters.p: The second index of the top call, shorted at 25,972.94.
Status after two sessions: the indices −3%, the single names much more.
Closed on 19 June with the SPX and NI225 shorts; all liquidity into Bitcoin spot.

ni225-short-2025-11.name: Nikkei 225
ni225-short-2025-11.lede: The first Nikkei short: 51,077 on 11 November 2025, ahead of the Bank of Japan, closed at 49,000 as the orders said — about +4%. “I was clear it was bearish, but also clear that better prices would come.”

chapters.h: Adding the Nikkei to the shorts at 51,077
chapters.p: Sold at 51,077 before the BOJ monetary policy meeting: the Japanese and American markets were the two most bearish in the world.

chapters.h: The thesis: BOJ hikes, the carry trade unwinds
chapters.p: The Bank of Japan set to raise rates through 2026; a very bearish Japanese market means a very bearish American market.

chapters.h: In writing: shorted at 51k, closed at 49k
chapters.p: “I initially gave orders to short the Japanese stock market at 51k and to close at 49k.” The second short was opened at 54k the same day.

ni225-short-2025-11.note: The close at 49,000 was confirmed on 14 January 2026; the exact day of the exit was not posted.

ni225-short-2026-01.name: Nikkei 225
ni225-short-2026-01.lede: The second Nikkei short, added at 54,340 on 14 January 2026 when “the better prices” arrived, and released at a small loss on 19 June with the US index shorts.

chapters.p: The 54k region was the solid level to add, rebalance risk and position for continuation; a 20% move down made sense from there.
“I now consider those better prices to be here.”
Closed with the SPX and NDX shorts on 19 June; all liquidity into Bitcoin spot.

intc-short-2026-04.name: Intel
intc-short-2026-04.lede: The last stock added to the short list: Intel at $93.26 on 29 April 2026, closed at a small loss on 19 June when every stock short was released for Bitcoin.

chapters.h: A new name on the short list: Intel at $93.26
chapters.p: On FOMC day, with the stock up 10% in a session, Intel was added to the shorts.
Released on 19 June with AMD, at a small loss.

orcl-spot-2026-07.name: Oracle
orcl-spot-2026-07.lede: Oracle bought at $140 on the Weekly MA200 on 6 July and sold at a small loss on 20 July: the chart was fine, the crowd's reaction to the OpenAI story was not. The only spot position of the summer that did not work.

chapters.h: Back at the Weekly MA200 — buying at $140 on Monday
chapters.p: A great long-term opportunity on the chart: the buy would go in at $140 as soon as the market opened.

chapters.h: Buy order filled at the MA200 weekly
chapters.p: Filled at $140 as planned. Long-term investment only.
With Oracle shorted to put pressure on OpenAI: “I am selling in small loss. Canceling the bets for now, even though long term the chart looks good, don't like the masses reaction.”

xrp-short-2025-09.name: XRP
xrp-short-2025-09.lede: A one-day hedge: XRP shorted at $3.0368 at 01:21 on 15 September 2025, expecting $2.90, and closed in profit at 22:03 the same day together with the LINK short. The exit price was not posted.

chapters.p: Opened as a hedge: the two shorts carried more sell pressure than the open longs, so the balance would grow whichever way Bitcoin went.
Twenty-one hours later: “Both shorts closed in profit. Leaving longs opened. $119,000.”

xrp-short-2025-09.note: Both hedges were closed in profit; the exit prices were not posted.

link-short-2025-09.name: Chainlink
link-short-2025-09.lede: A one-day hedge: LINK shorted at $24.19 at 01:22 on 15 September 2025, expecting $22.95, and closed in profit at 22:03 the same day with the XRP short. The exit price was not posted.

chapters.p: The second hedge of the night, one minute after XRP.
“Both shorts closed in profit. Leaving longs opened.”

link-short-2025-09.note: Both hedges were closed in profit; the exit prices were not posted.

bnb-long-2025-10.name: BNB
bnb-long-2025-10.lede: An intraday trade shared live: BNB long at 02:44 on 10 October 2025 targeting the 15-minute EMA200, take profit hit at 13:39. Entry and exit are on the charts posted; the prices were not written out.

chapters.h: Opening a long into the 15-minute EMA200
chapters.p: A short-term long with the EMA200 on the 15-minute chart as the take-profit region.
Eleven hours later the target was reached.

bnb-long-2025-10.note: Entry and exit as drawn on the posted charts; the prices were not written out.

sol-long-2025-10.name: Solana
sol-long-2025-10.lede: Opened going into the 29 October FOMC and added at $197 after the Powell dip; the position was back at breakeven the same night. The exit was not posted: the book was 40% cash and 50% short stocks by 14 November, so it was closed by then.

chapters.h: Opening a long going into FOMC
chapters.p: “Way too bullish chart.”
Twenty minutes after the rate cut, as Powell spoke, more was added at $197.
“I accept tips after TP hit.”

“I am holding one of the biggest retail positions, I am up 45%, and I am still regretting not having time to accumulate more.”
“Not selling till new ATH is made. Congratulations to everyone who bought.”

“There was to be no updates today. But has anyone noticed Palantir price action?”
